items.title: How has the Predators’ hot start affected their long-term roster vision?
items.summary: Second in the Central, the Preds have bought new GM Chris MacFarland time to evaluate all his pieces.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect After overhauling their front office last summer, the Nashville Predators have quietly been making a lot of changes to their roster – specifically up front. Headed by president of hockey operations and GM Chris MacFarland, the Predators have completely reshaped their offensive depth since the management changes. Bringing in forwards Mavrik Bourque, Ross Colton, Jack Drury, Nils Hoglander, Alex Kerfoot and, most recently, Shane Wright since the end of last season, there was sure to be an adjustment period for the group as head coach Andrew Brunette looked to integrate the new faces. Their respective individual impacts have been up and down but collectively have helped get the Predators off to what can be called an unexpected hot start. Winners of six games in a row and seven of their last 10, the Predators sit second in the ever-competitive Central Division as of Friday morning. With a new mix of forwards, the Predators have relied heavily on keeping pucks out of their net, currently averaging the fifth-fewest goals against per game in the NHL. It would’ve been safe to categorize the Predators as “soft sellers” after last season. Under former GM Barry Trotz, we heard the names of forwards Jonathan Marchessault, Ryan O’Reilly and Steven Stamkos on the trade block. And with a complete overhaul of the front office, a new set of eyes – a management group compiled from all around the NHL – would maybe want to put their fingerprints on the roster to a more significant degree than just shifting depth pieces. items.title: Jets place Dylan DeMelo on IR, recall Henry Thrun
items.body: Days after getting one veteran defenceman back, the Winnipeg Jets have lost another key blue-liner. Dylan DeMelo has been placed on injured reserve, the Jets announced Friday. He exited with a lower-body injury Thursday against the Dallas Stars. After the game, head coach Scott Arniel told reporters in Dallas that DeMelo will be week-to-week. The Jets just got Josh Morrissey back in the lineup earlier this week after an injury absence. The veteran blue-liner got his right leg caught under a falling Mikko Rantanen and went straight down the tunnel halfway through the first period. DeMelo had a goal and seven assists through 19 games entering Thursday. Henry Thrun has been recalled from AHL Manitoba to take DeMelo's place on the roster. He has one goal and six assists in 14 games with the Moose this season. Thrun played four games with the Toronto Maple Leafs last season and 55 with the AHL Marlies.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Winnipeg Jets will be without one of their best and most reliable defenseman for the time being, as the team announced on Friday morning that it has placed Dylan DeMelo on injured reserve. DeMelo suffered what appeared to be a leg injury when he got tangled up with Mikko Rantanen during the Jets’ 8-3 win over the Dallas Stars on Thursday night. DeMelo, 33, is in the midst of his 12th season in the NHL and his eighth as a member of the Jets. Through 19 games played this season, the veteran right-hander has notched eight points on one goal and seven assists while skating to a plus-3 rating on an average of 20:15 of time on ice per game. DeMelo was playing on Winnipeg’s top pairing on Thursday night alongside Josh Morrissey, who had just returned from his own injury. In a corresponding move, the Jets recalled defenseman Henry Thrun from their AHL affiliate Manitoba Moose. Thrun, 25, has 7 points in 14 games played with the Moose so far this season, and he has past NHL experience, mostly with the San Jose Sharks but most recently as a member of the Toronto Maple Leafs last year. items.title: NHL indicates Finland’s block on Russian athletes could affect future games there
items.body: The NHL will consider Finland's plans to prevent Russian athletes entering the country when deciding whether to stage more regular-season games there in future, the league told The Associated Press. Finland and Norway both announced plans to refuse entry to Russian athletes Thursday, the same day as the Carolina Hurricanes and Seattle Kraken played the first of two NHL regular-season games in the Finnish capital, Helsinki. The Finnish restrictions take effect from Monday, after the NHL games, and follow a backlash to Russia being reinstated in the hockey world championships, which is not an NHL event. “We are aware of the government’s position and we’ll have to take that into account," the league said on Friday when asked if the new restrictions would be an obstacle to future games in Finland. The Finnish foreign ministry's statement outlining the restrictions didn't distinguish between Russian athletes on national teams, those competing as neutral athletes, or those on club teams in sports like hockey or soccer. The ministry said Thursday that Russians would only be allowed to work in Finland on “tasks that are essential to Finland’s national interests." It added that Russia “uses sports as a propaganda tool.” The NHL has played regular-season games in Finland as part of its Global Series in 2022 and 2024 and hasn't confirmed any future games there yet. As of the opening day of the 2026-27 season in September, there were 53 Russians on NHL rosters, making up 7.3% of the league. That was the fourth-largest contingent of players from any country. Russian wing Andrei Svechnikov had an assist for the Hurricanes in Thursday's 4-1 win over the Kraken in Helsinki. Pyotr Kochetkov was Carolina's backup goaltender. items.title: Blackhawks proving to be NHL’s most curious rebuild
items.summary: Of all the rebuilding teams in the league, the Blackhawks just might be the toughest puzzle to solve. Why? Emily Sadler breaks it down.
items.body: This was supposed to be the year the Chicago Blackhawks finally took meaningful steps forward to emerge from their rebuild. And yet, a quarter of the way into the 2026-27 campaign, the team once again is stuck at the bottom of the standings. Chicago’s 3-2 overtime win against the Buffalo Sabres on Thursday, which snapped a six-game losing skid , was just their fifth victory over the season. Their 5-13-1 record has them sitting last in the tough Central Division by a wide margin, and second-last league-wide. General manager Kyle Davidson intended to make a statement with his off-season moves, trading the fourth-overall pick for cornerstone defenceman Bowen Byram and bringing back franchise icon Patrick Kane to be a veteran scoring presence for a young core up front. Instead, Davidson’s squad faces plenty of questions. Of the handful of teams at various stages of rebuilding, the Blackhawks might just be the toughest puzzle to solve and one of the most interesting teams to monitor as we enter the second quarter of the season. With all that in mind, we’re taking a closer look at the Blackhawks’ early-season woes, and the options ahead. While it’s still early, the numbers are troubling. Nineteen games into the season, the Blackhawks sit at or near the bottom of the league in just about every major statistical category. They’re last in goals scored per game, averaging 2.21 per matchup, and those scoring woes are compounded by a second-worst ranking in goals against per game (4.11). He had 12 points in 19 games with six of his eight goals coming in the Final. "We'll see how he feels tomorrow," coach Rod Brind'Amour said Friday. Staal played in the first six games of the season before he was injured during a morning skate on Oct. 10. Monahan’s absence would likely rotate Cole Sillinger back to the center position. It could also bring center Luca Del Bel Belluz back into the NHL lineup. items.title: Friday Four: How Hurricanes have become a model franchise
items.summary: The Carolina Hurricanes are a well-oiled machine. Michael Amato looks at how they became arguably the best blueprint of how to mould your franchise in the NHL.
items.body: If you ever watch a Carolina Hurricanes game, it looks less like an athletic competition and more like an operation or systematic dismantling of an opponent. The Canes are a well-oiled machine. Each part perfectly connected to the other and everyone pulling on the same rope. Once criticized as a team that couldn’t get over the hump, Carolina is now arguably the best blueprint of how to mould your franchise in the NHL. The Hurricanes' dominance was on full display during last year’s post-season. Carolina didn’t lose a game in the opening two rounds, allowing just 10 goals in a pair of sweeps. They would lose just three games en route to their second Stanley Cup and have picked up right where they left off in this 2026-27 season. The Canes have lost just twice in regulation since October 3rd and are on pace for a 134-point season. In a league powered by elite players, Carolina has done all this without a true superstar or a $10M player. There is such a belief in their system that it feels like they can mould almost any skater into an effective piece of their roster. Where other teams around the league crumble after being hit with adversity, the Hurricanes seem to thrive thanks to some foundational principles. You don’t achieve the consistency the Hurricanes have without utilizing incredible balance up and down your lineup. As mentioned earlier, Carolina doesn’t boast a true superstar. items.body: Forward packing it all in before finale against Kraken on Saturday The Seattle Kraken and Carolina Hurricanes have taken a break from their North American portion of the NHL schedule to play at Veikkaus Arena in Helsinki for the 2026 NHL Global Series Finland. The Carolina Hurricanes won the first game 4-1 on Thursday, the second game is Saturday (1 p.m. ET; HHN, Prime Video, CARNHL, KONG, KING, NHLN, SN1). Hurricanes forward Jesperi Kotkaniemi will keep a blog with NHL.com throughout the Global Series, giving fans a taste of what life is like on the ground as they go through the experience in Finland. Kotkaniemi’s third entry focuses on the victory Thursday, which was a Finnish showcase with teammate Sebastian Aho scoring twice and defenseman Juuso Valimaki also scoring. The Hurricanes took part in an open practice on Friday and Kotkaniemi also did meet-and-greet sessions with some children from a nearby hockey program. Last night was great. Just seeing a lot of familiar faces in the stands. It's kind of fun, you know, you kind of recognize who's Finnish and who's not in the stands. So, it was fun experience after a little while of being away from home. I think it was a good game for us, too. It was kind of a nice touch that Sebastian and Jusso each scored. items.body: TORONTO — As the Toronto Maple Leafs stumble toward the conclusion of what is already the worst six-game homestand in franchise history, Jim Hiller struck a frightening tone. The head coach of this 8-11-2 outfit didn’t point fingers at underachieving offensive stars or struggling defencemen. He didn’t chastise or fume or waste time addressing his frustrated skaters after a fifth consecutive regulation home loss — the worst such stretch for the Leafs since a 1990-91 group that finished dead last in the Campbell Conference. “I see lots of hope. I see it. I see it all over the place. I really do,” Hiller said, following a 5-2 loss to the juggernaut Minnesota Wild. The Maple Leafs have more regulation losses (11) than anyone in their conference. They’ve been outscored 22-9 during a homestand from hell. They can’t play two of their best defencemen because one (Morgan Rielly) is dealing with an injury and the other (Chris Tanev) is susceptible to one . And the vengeful Edmonton Oilers have already loaded their bags into Scotiabank Arena, resting up for a Saturday showdown. Knowing he can’t take a hammer to a team gone fragile, Hiller spoke about the virtues of his bottom-line grinders, who were only on for one goal against versus Minnesota and have provided some noticeable pop during the slump. "So, we talk about hope. Hey, these guys are playing outstanding. Rule 38.1 states, “In all Coach’s Challenge situations, the original call on the ice will be overturned if, and only if, a conclusive and irrefutable determination can be made on the basis of video evidence that the original call on the ice was clearly not correct. If a review is not conclusive and/or there is any doubt whatsoever as to whether the call on the ice was correct, the original call on the ice will be confirmed.” Video review determined that St. Louis’ Mason McTavish preceded the puck into the offensive zone and was in an off-side position prior to his goal . According to Rule 38.9, “The standard for overturning the call in the event of a “GOAL” call on the ice is that the NHL Situation Room, after reviewing any and all available replays and consulting with the On-Ice Official(s), determines that one or more Players on the attacking team preceded the puck into the attacking zone prior to the goal being scored and that, as a result, the play should have been stopped for an “Off-Side” infraction; where this standard is met, the goal will be disallowed.” The clock is reset to show 5:28 (14:32 elapsed time), when the off-side infraction occurred.

items.body: Mark Scheifele has officially tied his mentor as the greatest scorer in Winnipeg Jets history. Scheifele had two goals and an assist in Thursday's 8-3 win over the Dallas Stars to tie Dale Hawerchuk for the most points in Winnipeg Jets history. Scheifele now has 929 points, the same total Hawerchuk had with the original Jets. The two goals Thursday gave Scheifele 378 goals in his career, one behind Hawerchuk's 379 for the most in franchise history. The milestone comes after the NHL announced this summer that statistics from Jets 1.0 and 2.0 are now merged, something made possible after the Arizona Coyotes went dormant in 2024. Scheifele was the first-ever draft pick by Jets 2.0 after moving to Winnipeg from Atlanta in 2011. Since then, he has been a consistent offensive star for the Jets over his 14 NHL seasons, including scoring a career-high 103 points last season. This season, he has 22 points in 20 games. Before being drafted by the Jets, Scheifele played under Hawerchuk when the Jets legend coached the OHL's Barrie Colts. The two formed a bond that continued as Scheifele moved to Winnipeg. Hawerchuk played nine of the 16 seasons in his Hall of Fame career with Jets 1.0 from 1981 to 1990. He died of cancer in 2020 at age 57.

Detroit led 4-1 with less than 30 seconds left in the second period, but from there, it was all Florida. Lars Eller, Gustav Forsling and Sam Reinhart also scored for the Panthers, and Carter Verhaeghe had three assists. Andreas Englund got his first goal in more than two years, Marco Kasper also had his first of the season, and Lucas Raymond and J.T. Compher also scored for Detroit. Moritz Seider had two assists, but the Red Wings lost their fifth straight. Reinhart’s goal was 3:52 into the game — his 200th with the Panthers — and gave Florida a 1-0 lead, but Detroit scored the next four. It was only the third instance of a 4-0 run in a game by Detroit this season, and it still wasn't enough. Englund’s third career goal was his first since Oct. 17, 2024, at Montreal — and his other goal, in 2023, was at Toronto. He hadn’t scored in 85 games on U.S. soil before Thursday. Kasper’s goal just past the midpoint of the second period pushed the Detroit lead to 4-1, prompting some boos from an impatient home crowd. Forsling scored with 18 seconds left in the second to get Florida within two, and Lundell connected 2:32 into the third to make it 4-3. items.title: Canadiens snap Bruins’ seven-game home win streak
items.body: BOSTON — Josh Anderson and Jake Evans each had a goal and an assist as the Montreal Canadiens leapfrogged the Boston Bruins in the Atlantic Division standings with a 5-2 win on Thursday night. Now 9-0-3 in its past 12 games, Montreal came in trailing Boston by one point for the top spot in the division. Kirby Dach, Cole Caufield and Phillip Danault also scored for the Canadiens, who improved to 10–0–2 when leading after two periods. Jacob Fowler had 30 saves. Boston’s seven-game winning streak on home ice was snapped. Jeremy Swayman was pulled after allowing four goals on 17 shots and was replaced by Michael DiPietro, who made 13 saves. Casey Mittelstadt scored both of Boston’s goals and the Bruins outshot Montreal, 32-30. Dach opened the scoring with a wraparound goal at 2:34 into the contest. He skated behind Swayman with a long reach enabling Dach to finish it himself for his second of the season. Montreal took a 2-0 lead in the first period when Anderson planted himself in front of Swayman and deflected in a rebound for his eighth goal of the season. The Canadiens extended their two-goal cushion when Evans went scored on a breakaway after taking a pass from Anderson. Montreal ended Swayman’s night at 11:46 of the second period when Caufield fired a shot from just outside the left circle into the top corner. Swayman’s early exit and subsequent replacement by DiPietro marked the first time this season that Boston made an in-game change at goalie. Boston got on the scoreboard after Danault scored on a long one-timer from the top of the right circle that made it 5-0. Mittelstadt made a backhand move for his first of two goals. items.title: Hellebuyck makes 26 saves as Devils beat Capitals
items.body: NEWARK, N.J. — Vladislav Kolyachonok scored the go-ahead goal early in the third period and Connor Hellebuyck made 26 saves as the New Jersey Devils beat the Washington Capitals 5-2 on Thursday night in the first of a two-game set. Kolyachonok’s shot trickled past Capitals goaltender Logan Thompson at 6:27. It was the first game in a Devils uniform for the 25-year-old defenseman, who signed in July as a free agent. He was in the lineup in place of the injured Johnathan Kovacevic. Evan Rodrigues, Lenni Hameenaho, Stefan Noesen and Jack Hughes also scored for the Devils, who have won seven straight home games. Hellebuyck returned to the ice after the Devils held him out of Tuesday's loss at Winnipeg, the team that traded him to New Jersey last month. Hellebuyck was booed by Jets fans and said incidents involving his family had prompted his demand to be traded. He has won his first six starts with New Jersey. The Devils are 12-3-0 in their last 15 games and 9-2-0 overall at Prudential Center. Ryan Leonard and Pierre-Luc Dubois scored for the Capitals, who had their two-game winning streak stopped. Thompson stopped 24 shots. Rodrigues opened the scoring on the power play 2:20 into the first. Leonard tied it on the power play later in the period. Dubois put the Capitals ahead early in the second. Hameenaho knotted the score 2-2 with his first goal this season, deflecting Brendan Dillon's shot past Thompson. Noesen scored at 17:07 of the third, and Hughes had an empty-netter. The Devils, who missed the playoffs last season, are second in the Metropolitan Division with 28 points.

items.title: Maple Leafs fall to Wild for fifth straight home loss
items.body: Matt Boldy completed his second hat trick of the season and the sixth of his career early in the third period as the Minnesota Wild resigned the Toronto Maple Leafs to a fifth straight regulation home loss with a 5-2 victory Thursday. Boldy's third goal of the night came after Maple Leafs winger William Nylander and defenceman Oliver Ekman-Larsson got their wires crossed off the rush to open a clear lane for the Wild winger. Michael McCarron and Danila Yurov, into an empty net, also scored for Minnesota (14-3-4), which got 26 saves from Jesper Wallstedt. Kirill Kaprizov had three assists. Yurov added an assist for a two-point night. The Maple Leafs (8-11-2) have lost the first of five contests of what has turned into a disastrous six-game homestand to move to an ugly 1-7-0 over their last eight. The Wild improved to 8-0-2 over their last 10 since last losing in regulation to the Calgary Flames on Oct. 22. Maple Leafs: Veteran defenceman Chris Tanev (load management) was kept out of the lineup for the second time in three games. Fellow blueliner Morgan Rielly (lower body) remains on the club's long list of injured players. Wild: Brock Faber could return to action this weekend after the blueliner suffered a fractured skull during pre-season play. Toronto defenceman Darren Raddysh took a penalty midway through the second that led to Boldy tying the game 2-2 on a power play. Quinn Hughes picked up an assist on Boldy's second to give the Minnesota defenceman a point streak of at least 10 games for the third time in his career. That ties Phil Housley for the second-most by an American blueliner in NHL history. Brian Leetch tops the list with four.

items.body: The Montreal Canadiens lost forward Chris Kreider to an apparent injury in the third period of Thursday's game against the Boston Bruins. Kreider was sent down the tunnel with less than 14 minutes remaining in the third period after Bruins forward Michael Eyssimont fell at the centre-ice line and slid into the veteran's knee. The 35-year-old Kreider stayed down the ice after the awkward collision and officials whistled the play down almost immediately. Kreider couldn't put any weight on his left leg as he limped to the nearby Canadiens bench and to the locker room. Kreider entered Thursday's contest with three goals and six assists in 18 games. This is his first season with Montreal after joining the club on a one-year contract in September. He had played with the New York Rangers for the first 13 years of his career before suiting up for the Anaheim Ducks in 2025-26.

items.body: Explanation: The play on the ice was challenged under Rule 38 – Coach’s Challenge. Rule 38.1 states, “In all Coach’s Challenge situations, the original call on the ice will be overturned if, and only if, a conclusive and irrefutable determination can be made on the basis of video evidence that the original call on the ice was clearly not correct. If a review is not conclusive and/or there is any doubt whatsoever as to whether the call on the ice was correct, the original call on the ice will be confirmed.” Video review determined that Winnipeg’s Cole Perfetti preceded the puck into the offensive zone and was in an off-side position prior to Kyle Connor’s goal . According to Rule 38.9, “The standard for overturning the call in the event of a “GOAL” call on the ice is that the NHL Situation Room, after reviewing any and all available replays and consulting with the On-Ice Official(s), determines that one or more Players on the attacking team preceded the puck into the attacking zone prior to the goal being scored and that, as a result, the play should have been stopped for an “Off-Side” infraction; where this standard is met, the goal will be disallowed.” The clock is reset to show 3:32 (16:28 elapsed time), when the off-side infraction occurred.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Columbus Blue Jackets were without their head coach for Thursday’s game against the Tampa Bay Lightning , as Rick Bowness missed the match due to an illness. Bowness had missed the team’s morning skate earlier on Thursday, with the Blue Jackets confirmed that it was due to an illness. His status wasn’t confirmed for the game, but the team announced a half hour before puck drop that he would miss the game. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Pablo Robles-Imagn Images The Tampa Bay Lightning will be down a couple of key pieces for Thursday’s road game against the Columbus Blue Jackets . Speaking before Thursday’s game, Lightning head coach Jon Cooper revealed that forward Anthony Cirelli and defenseman Erik Cernak will not play against the Blue Jackets. During an appearance on NHL Network’s NHL Tonight with host Tony Luftman, the former Washington Capitals head coach recently shared his thoughts on the upcoming candidacy of several former NHLers, making it clear that he would love to see Backstrom receive hockey’s highest individual honor. “I, certainly, for me, would love to see Nick get in,” Boudreau said. “I’d love to see Ryan Getzlaf get in and Eric Staal – three guys that I’ve coached that are all on the potential list. But it is our most basic human nature to take shelter from the elements, and you’d be surprised how many Vancouver Canuck players over the decades were easy to find after wins, when it was sunny, but impossible to locate when it was raining. Right now, it is absolutely pouring on the Canucks, who reach the one-quarter mark of their rebuild season on Friday carrying not only the worst 20-game record in franchise history (3-16-1) but one of the worst on record with the National Hockey League. items.title: Blackhawks’ Patrick Kane activated from IR, expected to return vs. Sabres
items.summary: Kane has missed the last few games due to an upper-body injury, bringing some spark to a struggling team.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Jerome Miron-USA TODAY Sports Showtime is back in action in the Windy City. On Thursday, the Chicago Blackhawks activated forward Patrick Kane from injured reserve. With that, he’s expected to be in the lineup for that night’s game, as the Blackhawks are set to play host to the Buffalo Sabres . Kane’s return seemed imminent, as he has been practicing with the main group for the past couple of days. He has missed the past three games after suffering an upper-body injury last Monday against the Colorado Avalanche . He left the contest, which saw the Hawks lose to the Avs by a final score of 5-2, in the second period. He was later placed on IR . This is the first game Kane was eligible to return to the lineup, as Chicago hasn’t played since suffering a 9-2 drubbing at the hands of the defending Stanley Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes last Saturday. With Kane out, Chicago extended its losing streak, which is now up to six games. Kane has been one of the Hawks’ more productive players so far this season, though that isn’t saying much. The 37-year-old has a goal and eight assists for nine points in 15 contests, placing him second on the team in helpers behind Connor Bedard, and third in overall scoring behind Bedard and Roman Kantserov. Kane has a plus/minus of -15 while averaging just over 18 minutes of ice time per game. The Blackhawks (4-13-1) are last in the Central Division, two points ahead of the Vancouver Canucks for the worst record in the NHL and 12 points back of the last Wild Card spot in the Western Conference.

items.body: HELSINKI — Sebastian Aho scored twice in front of the home crowd and the Carolina Hurricanes opened the NHL’s Global Series in the Finnish capital with a 4-1 victory over the Seattle Kraken on Thursday. Left winger Taylor Hall celebrated his 1,000th NHL game in the reigning Stanley Cup champions' victorious return to Helsinki’s Veikkaus Arena after 16 years. Nikolaj Ehlers had a goal and an assist, and Aho's fellow Finn, defenceman Juuso Välimäki, also scored for the Hurricanes (15-3-2) who have won seven of their last eight games. The dominant Hurricanes jumped to a 2-0 with the goals coming just 1:06 apart in the opening period. Ehlers put them 1-0 up with 8:16 remaining with a wrist shot from the blue line. Home crowd hero Aho doubled the advantage on a power play moments later after he was fed at the side of the net by Blake. He made it 4-0 on a one-timer from the slot in the final period. The Finnish scoring leader for the Hurricanes has three goals and seven points in the last three games. With his 321st career goal, Aho tied Olli Jokinen for the fourth place among Finnish players in NHL history. Frederick Gaudreau scored the lone goal for Seattle (9-7-1) and Philipp Grubauer finished with 26 saves. The 34-year-old Hall became the first player to skate his 1,000th game overseas. In his 17th NHL season, Hall has 305 goals and 488 assists for a total of 793 points. The Los Angeles Kings announced that forward Kevin Fiala is set to make his 2026-27 season debut on Thursday night, as the Kings host the New York Islanders . Fiala has been out of action since suffering a gruesome leg injury while representing Switzerland at the 2026 Winter Olympics. The injury led him to undergo surgery that knocked him out for the rest of the 2025-26 season. Fiala also missed training camp and the first month of the new campaign while recovering. The 30-year-old will be a welcome addition to the lineup, as the Kings have struggled through the first quarter of the year. Through 16 games, Los Angeles has scored just 45 goals, which ranks 30th in the NHL. They also have a goal differential of -10, tied for 24th in the league. Fiala has been one of the Kings’ top scoring threats since he joined the organization in 2022. After posting consecutive 70-point campaigns, he registered 60 points in 81 games during the 2024-25 season. He was on pace to reach 60 points again last year before the injury, as Fiala had notched 18 goals and 40 points in 56 games prior to the Olympic Break. In 707 regular-season games in the NHL, Fiala has posted 229 goals and 299 assists for 528 points, with another 30 points in 49 Stanley Cup Playoff contests. Fiala is in the fifth season of the six-year contract extension, which he signed in June 2022. The deal carries an AAV of $7.875 million and includes a modified no-trade clause. items.body: First-ever Finnish-born goalie to make Hockey Hall of Fame does honors CAR@SEA: Rinne joins Aho and Kakko for the ceremonial puck drop in Finland An adoring crowd in Helsinki welcomed Pekka Rinne with a rousing ovation just before he dropped the ceremonial puck at the 2026 NHL Global Series Finland at Veikkaus Arena in Helsinki on Thursday. Rinne, who became the first ever Finnish-born goalie inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame earlier this week, did the honors ahead of the game between the defending Stanley Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes and Seattle Kraken. He was inducted to the Hockey Hall on Monday as part of the Class of 2026 alongside NHL players Carey Price , Patrice Bergeron , Keith Tkachuk and women's player Cindy Curley. Longtime executive Brian Burke was inducted as a builder. Rinne, who hails from Kempele, was on hand to do the honors in Helsinki for the special event. Instead of the captains taking the honorary faceoff, a pair of Rinne's Finnish countrymen did the honors: Hurricanes forward Sebastian Aho , from Rauma and Kraken forward Kaapo Kakko , a native of Turku. Rinne played 15 NHL seasons and posted 369 career wins, tied for 22nd most in NHL history. He won the Vezina Trophy 2018 and the King Clancy Trophy in 2021. His 2.43 goals-against average is 20th best in League history and career .917 save percentage is 14th all-time.

items.title: Sedins unhappy with Canucks’ results, weighing options amid dismal season
items.body: Daniel and Henrik Sedin say they're not happy with the Vancouver Canucks ' results, but they believe in their coaching staff and players. The NHL team's co-presidents of hockey operations spoke to reporters on Thursday about the beleaguered club, which sits at the bottom of the league standings with a 3-16-1 record. The Canucks have lost six straight games and 16 of their last 17. Daniel Sedin says they're evaluating players every day but have yet to see the group put together a full, consistent effort over an entire game. His twin brother, Henrik Sedin, says Vancouver's front office is "looking at all players" to see what options are available for improving the team, but that the Canucks won't simply trade top talent away to get more draft picks because they need players who can produce on the ice and support up-and-coming athletes. The Sedins played their entire 17-season NHL careers in Vancouver and were appointed the team's co-presidents of hockey operations in May after the Canucks finished the 2025-26 season last in the league.

On Thursday, the team announced that defenseman Mike Matheson will be back in the lineup for that night’s game, which will see the Canadiens pay a visit to the rival Boston Bruins. With Matheson out of the lineup, the Canadiens have done well, going 4-0-2, though the team lost to the Minnesota Wild in overtime this past Tuesday night. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Marc DesRosiers-Imagn Some reinforcements are returning to the nation’s capital. Following the team’s morning skate, it was revealed that Ottawa Senators goaltender Linus Ullmark has been activated from injured reserve and will be starting on Thursday night, when the Senators host the Colorado Avalanche. Ullmark has missed the past nine games due to a lower-body injury s uffered during a game on Oct. 21 against the Florida Panthers . He was quickly placed on IR, with Ottawa riding Samuel Ersson throughout his absence. Ullmark has missed the past nine games, with the Sens doing okay without him, going 4-3-2 after losing to the Washington Capitals this past Tuesday night. Yet, the Sens remain in the thick of the hunt for a Stanley Cup Playoff spot. The return of the Swedish backstop will certainly help Ottawa, as Ullmark has been exceptional in his limited action this year. In eight starts, he has posted a record of 7-1-0, with a 1.33 goals-against average and a .945 save percentage. His lone loss came at the hands of the Philadelphia Flyers back on Oct. 17. For Ottawa fans, seeing Ullmark injured has become the norm since he was dealt to the team in 2024. While he’s played at least over half of the games in each of his first two seasons, he has been on and off the injured list, along with taking a personal leave of absence last season. He’s already missed some time this year, as an injury against the Boston Bruins earlier this month knocked him out for one game. Yet, when he’s in between the pipes, few players have had a greater impact on the Sens than he. We've entered a new era of development for NHL-drafted players out of the CHL. Not only has the NCAA pathway been opened up to them, but this is the first year in which each team is able to assign one of their 19-year-old CHLers to play in the AHL. We've occasionally seen European teenagers get the chance to make the move to the AHL and it's always been viewed as a very solid place to develop those players. This year, the crop of 19-year-olds in the AHL look quite solid and there is a very strong likelihood that we see most of them at the world junior hockey championship in just over a month. More Videos Let's check in on the top teenage talent in the AHL. The physical Russian center is looking more and more like the player we saw in his D-1 season, where he was viewed as a potential top-five pick. Ryabkin is a heat-seaking missile who also brings impressive hands and skill with the puck. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Nick Wosika-Imagn Images Usually, when a player says that he wants to leave a team, he will sulk and trudge through games, or simply not play at all. It was just a couple of weeks ago that the Tampa Bay Lightning legend made a trade request, as he reportedly wouldn’t re-sign with the only team he has ever known. While the announcement sent shockwaves through the league, it did little to deter the 33-year-old’s play. In the six games since the news broke, Kucherov has been on fire, scoring five goals and 11 points across six games, including a hat trick against the Buffalo Sabres on Wednesday night. On Thursday’s edition of Daily Faceoff LIVE , Tyler Yaremchuk and Carter Hutton break down Kucherov’s incredible play since it came out that he wanted out of town. Carter Hutton: It’s been a show of talent so far, and I think this is one of those where you kind of kick the hornet’s nest, this is what you’re going to get. He was pretty clear about how he felt the way that he was treated, and it wasn’t about the money; it was about the disrespect. I think that factor is, now, he is playing with that edge and that fire, and there’s different players are motivated in different ways, and you have to find ways to do it. I think that’s what we’re seeing right now from Kucherov, is the fact that he’s motivated to be the best possible player that he can be, and to show BriseBois and his team he’s not turning on them, he’s not checking out, he’s just going to use this as fuel. Right now is a great example of a team that went into Buffalo and just absolutely waxed them last night. That is a big win and a statement win for the Lightning.

"It's really to give them that great experience," NHL vice president of international operations Mark Black said. "For some of them, it's going to be their first experience with hockey, and we just want to make it a memorable experience for them. Obviously, for the teachers, it's a good opportunity to get the kids outdoors, looking for additional things, so we're always grateful for the schools and the teachers to bring their kids out. "For us, it's to give kids who know hockey the opportunity to engage with the NHL, but certainly for the kids who don't have hockey experience relevant to them, it gives them their first hockey experience." items.summary: Sidney Crosby, Wayne Gretzky, Jimmy Carson and Mario Lemieux are the only players to hit the milestone at a younger age.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Bob Kupbens-Imagn Images Macklin Celebrini has found himself in rare air. During the San Jose Sharks ‘ 3-2 shootout loss to the Pittsburgh Penguins on Wednesday , Celebrini hit the 200-point milestone in his career, becoming the fifth-youngest player to reach that threshold. Celebrini achieved the feat midway through the third period of the game, when an offensive zone sequence saw Will Smith pass the puck across the zone to Michael Kesselring, who had previously pinched up on the breakout rush and was still deep in the zone. Kesselring immediately bumped the puck towards Celebrini in the high slot, who faked the first shot to trick the defense and goalie before firing home a goal to cut Pittsburgh’s 2-1 lead in half and giving him his 200th career point. Celebrini then followed it up with the primary assist on Mason Marchment’s game-tying goal with a bit over four minutes to go in the third period, giving him his 201st point. With his 200th point, Celebrini became the fifth-youngest player to reach the milestone, doing so at the age of 20 years and 151 days. He joins some elite players in the process, with the four players ahead of him being Mario Lemieux (20 years, 133 days), Jimmy Carson (20 years, 107 days), Wayne Gretzky (19 years, 347 days) and Sidney Crosby (19 years, 207 days). Admittedly, Celebrini and Crosby do have an advantage to get there in a similar amount of time to the likes of Gretzky and Lemieux, as the two have birthdays closer to the cut-off date for draft eligibility, with Celebrini’s being June 13th and Crosby’s being August 7th.
